messages.subject: colwise row names
parts:
A couple of micro-suggestions: 

1) have colwise(f)(df) have the same rownames as sapply(df,f)

Compare:

> df <- data.frame(a=rnorm(100),b=runif(100))
> colwise(function(x)quantile(x,0:4/4))(df)
            a           b
1 -2.71176028 0.003217725
2 -0.62321472 0.228328591
3 -0.08124694 0.498986807
4  0.65992414 0.758194742
5  2.46854110 0.995497320

> sapply(df,function(x)quantile(x,0:4/4))
               a           b
0%   -2.71176028 0.003217725
25%  -0.62321472 0.228328591
50%  -0.08124694 0.498986807
75%   0.65992414 0.758194742
100%  2.46854110 0.995497320

2) Have colwise(f,...)(df) do R-style currying like sapply(df,f,...)

cf.

> sapply(df,quantile,0:4/4)

messages.subject: Re: colwise row names
parts:
I really dislike rownames, and all plyr functions currently drop them.
It might be useful to have an option to add them as a new column
though.

> 2) Have colwise(f,...)(df) do R-style currying like sapply(df,f,...)
> cf.
>> sapply(df,quantile,0:4/4)

Hmmm, this is a bit tricky because you'd need to integrate two sets of
arguments: colwise(f, ...)(df, ...)

messages.subject: Re: colwise row names
parts: On Tue, Oct 11, 2011 at 09:56, Hadley Wickham <had...@rice.edu> wrote:

> A couple of micro-suggestions:
> 1) have colwise(f)(df) have the same rownames as sapply(df,f)...

I really dislike rownames, and all plyr functions currently drop them.
 It might be useful to have an option to add them as a new column
though.

> 2) Have colwise(f,...)(df) do R-style currying like sapply(df,f,...)
> cf.
>> sapply(df,quantile,0:4/4)

Hmmm, this is a bit tricky because you'd need to integrate two sets of
arguments: colwise(f, ...)(df, ...)

Something like this, maybe? 

colwise <- 
function (.fun, ..., .cols = true) 
{
    if (!is.function(.cols)) {
        .cols <- as.quoted(.cols)
        filter <- function(df) eval.quoted(.cols, df)
    }
    else {
        filter <- function(df) Filter(.cols, df)
    }
    outerargs = list(...)
    function(df, ...) {
        stopifnot(is.data.frame(df))
        filtered <- filter(df)
        if (length(filtered) == 0) 
            return(data.frame())
        df <- quickdf(do.call(lapply,c(list(filtered, .fun), outerargs,...)))
        names(df) <- names(filtered)
        df
    }
}
